result.title: Checkpoint Reload Explains Most of the Measured State Gap in Two State Discovery Reproductions
result.comment: Equal contribution, 11 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Temporal Systems (FMTS 2026). Equal contribution
result.summary: Temporal models that maintain per-sequence latent states during training must reconstruct those states when the stored table is unavailable at inference. This creates a basic consistency question: do the reconstructed states agree with those formed during training? We study this question for State Discovery in World Machine, which updates stored states in parallel each epoch but performs inference by sequential rollout from an all-zero start. On Toy1D, we analyze two paired-checkpoint runs whose decoded-state MSE is 27 to 36 percent above the published value. We compare the stored table with rollouts under the best-validation checkpoint reloaded after training and the last-epoch weights that wrote the table. Matching the rollout to the table-writing weights removes 90 to 91 percent of the mean per-dimension Wasserstein-1 distance. Causal distillation and frozen SD updates do not satisfy their pre-specified criteria under either checkpoint. Overall, checkpoint reload accounts for most of the measured gap in these runs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文复现 World Machine 中 State Discovery 的状态一致性：在两个配对检查点运行上，将存储的状态表与重载最佳验证检查点、最后轮次权重后的顺序 rollout 对比，发现用写入状态表的权重可消除九成左右的 Wasserstein-1 距离，而因果蒸馏与冻结状态更新均未达预设标准。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文关于训练期存储 latent 状态与推理期 rollout 重建状态是否一致、以及检查点选择如何污染状态差距测量的诊断，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 相似度与状态一致性度量被权重版本、缓存或深度设置混淆的可能。
